title: Acoustic analysis of pharyngealization and vowel duration in L2 Arabic by German learners
reason: The production study otherwise meets the manual-measurement standard, but its data availability statement explicitly says the generated/analyzed data are not publicly available because participants did not consent to external sharing.
evidence: Twenty speakers produced Arabic short/long vowels in plain and emphatic contexts; target tokens were phonetically transcribed by the researcher and an experienced speech-language pathologist, and automatically extracted F1/F2 values were manually corrected at vowel midpoint. The article explicitly states that underlying data are confidential and not publicly available.
lineage_action: Retain citation as methodological/source-discovery evidence only; do not ingest participant measurements unless a future public consented release appears.
